headline: New South Wales Government Shelves Real Estate Underquoting Laws
seoTitle: NSW Shelves Underquoting Real Estate Laws
metaDescription: The New South Wales government has cancelled planned real estate reforms aimed at underquoting just one day before they were scheduled to commence.
aiSummaryBullets: The New South Wales government delayed new legislation intended to address property price underquoting.
Real estate agents expressed concerns to the premier regarding the potential impact of the regulations on the local housing market.
The cancelled requirements included mandatory property price advertising or specific price range disclosures.
aiContextParagraph: The government of New South Wales, led by Premier Chris Minns, decided to halt the implementation of new real estate regulations just one day before they were set to take effect. These measures were originally designed to protect homebuyers by preventing underquoting, a practice where agents advertise properties at prices lower than the expected sale amount. However, following feedback from real estate agents within his own electorate regarding the potential consequences of these rules during a housing market downturn, the Premier opted to abandon the policy. This decision is one of several legislative retreats made by the government in recent weeks as the state moves toward an election scheduled for March. The shelved reforms would have included mandatory requirements for agents to publicly list selling prices or established price ranges for homes on the market.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained moderate traction through coverage from major national outlets including The Guardian and the ABC.
